examples.normal: The teacher gave her a lot of praise for her work.
examples.hard: A little praise from your manager can make a hard week feel much easier.

examples.normal: We had an excellent meal at the new restaurant, and the prices were good too.
examples.hard: She got excellent results in her exams because she studied every evening for months.

examples.normal: We had an amazing holiday by the sea last summer.
examples.hard: It is amazing how quickly children learn a new language when they live abroad.

examples.normal: The new bridge was built in an astonishing six months.
examples.hard: The young pianist played with astonishing skill, and the whole audience stood up to clap.

examples.normal: Thank you for a wonderful dinner. The food was great.
examples.hard: My grandmother was a wonderful cook, and her kitchen always smelt of fresh bread.

examples.normal: Their new singer has a sensational voice and a lot of fans.
examples.hard: The team had a sensational season, winning almost every match they played at home.

examples.normal: We stayed in a fabulous hotel with a big swimming pool.
examples.hard: The party was fabulous, with great music, delicious food and lots of old friends.

examples.normal: Well done! You passed your driving test on the first try.
examples.hard: When I finished my first marathon, my wife hugged me and said, "Well done, I'm so proud of you."

examples.normal: Good job! Your homework has no mistakes this time.
examples.hard: The manager told the new workers they had done a good job and could go home early.

examples.normal: My sister is a brilliant doctor, and her patients love her.
examples.hard: He is a brilliant student, but he sometimes forgets to hand in his homework on time.

examples.normal: This word is new, so write it down in your notebook.
examples.hard: If you don't write it down straight away, you will probably forget the phone number by tomorrow.

examples.easy: Here's my number. Jot it down.
examples.normal: I have a good idea, so let me jot it down.
examples.hard: Keep a small notebook in your bag, and when you hear a useful word, jot it down.

examples.normal: You can erase pencil marks easily, but not pen marks.
examples.hard: I accidentally erased all the photos on my phone, so I lost the pictures from our holiday.

examples.normal: We use 'is' with a singular noun, like 'the car is'.
examples.hard: In English, a singular noun usually needs a word like 'a' or 'the' in front of it.

examples.normal: The plural of 'child' is 'children', not 'childs'.
examples.hard: Most English nouns form the plural with -s, but some common words, like 'man' and 'woman', are irregular.

examples.normal: She is a student at a university in Tashkent.
examples.hard: As a student, he worked in a café in the evenings to pay for his books.

examples.normal: We walk our dog in the park every morning.
examples.hard: Our neighbours have a big dog that barks loudly whenever someone walks past their gate.

examples.normal: I work in an office and go home at six.
examples.hard: I have studied English for two years, but I still want to speak more fluently.

examples.normal: Are you a teacher or a student at this school?
examples.hard: If you need help with your homework, you can call me at any time this evening.

examples.normal: He is a doctor, and he works in a big hospital.
examples.hard: He lives near the station, so he usually walks to work instead of taking the bus.

examples.normal: She is my sister, and she lives in Samarkand.
examples.hard: She speaks three languages, and she wants to work for an international company one day.

examples.normal: I have a cat. It is black and very small.
examples.hard: I bought a new phone last week, and it takes much better photos than my old one.

examples.normal: We live in a small flat near the city centre.
examples.hard: We usually visit our parents on Sundays and have a big family lunch together.

examples.normal: They are doctors, and they work in the same hospital.
examples.hard: They moved to London last year, and now they want to buy a house there.

examples.normal: We use a pronoun so we don't repeat the same name.
examples.hard: In the sentence 'Anna is a nurse and she works at night', the word 'she' is a pronoun.

examples.normal: English has seven personal pronouns, like 'I', 'you' and 'they'.
examples.hard: Every English sentence needs a subject, and very often that subject is a personal pronoun such as 'he'.

examples.normal: Our English teacher gives us homework after every lesson.
examples.hard: The teacher explained the new rule twice, so that everyone in the class could understand it.

examples.normal: If you feel ill, you should go to the doctor.
examples.hard: The doctor told him to drink more water and to rest at home for three days.

examples.normal: The nurse checked my temperature and gave me some water.
examples.hard: My aunt has worked as a nurse in the children's hospital for more than twenty years.

examples.normal: My son wants to be a famous football player one day.
examples.hard: The football player hurt his leg in the first half, so he could not finish the match.

examples.normal: I have a toothache, so I need to see a dentist.
examples.hard: You should visit the dentist twice a year, even if your teeth don't hurt.

examples.normal: She is a hardworking student and always does her homework.
examples.hard: My parents are hardworking people who started their own small business with very little money.

examples.normal: My brother drives his car to work every day.
examples.hard: We want to buy a bigger car, because our old one is too small for the family.

examples.normal: The pilot said, "Welcome on board. We are flying to Istanbul."
examples.hard: My cousin trained for three years to become a pilot, and now she flies all over the world.

examples.normal: I always keep a small umbrella in my bag in spring.
examples.hard: I left my umbrella on the bus this morning, so I got completely wet on the way home.

examples.normal: A billionaire bought the old football club last year.
examples.hard: The billionaire gave a lot of money to build new schools and hospitals in poor areas.

examples.normal: The businessman travels to Dubai three or four times a year.
examples.hard: He started as a shop assistant, but now he is a successful businessman with ten shops.

examples.normal: A porter at the station helped me with my heavy suitcase.
examples.hard: When we arrived at the hotel, a friendly porter took our luggage up to the fifth floor.

examples.normal: I have dinner with my family every Sunday evening.
examples.hard: My family lives in Bukhara, but I moved to Tashkent for work three years ago.

examples.normal: He is a smart boy, and he learns new things quickly.
examples.hard: She is smart enough to fix the computer herself, so she never pays for repairs.

units.name: Lesson 2 - Countries and verb to be

examples.normal: Yes, I am a student at the language centre.
examples.hard: My brother is a student in Moscow, and he comes home every summer.

examples.normal: "Is she from Canada?" "Yes, she is. She's from Toronto."
examples.hard: When the manager asked if I could work on Saturday, I said yes without thinking.

examples.normal: Our teacher is from England, and she is very friendly.
examples.hard: The new teacher speaks slowly and clearly, so all the students understand her easily.

examples.normal: "Are you from Japan?" "No, I'm not. I'm from Turkey."
examples.hard: I asked my boss for a day off next week, but unfortunately he said no.

examples.normal: Where is your teacher from? Is she from England?
examples.hard: Where do you usually go on holiday when you want a quiet week by the sea?

examples.normal: My new friend is from Canada, but she lives in Tashkent.
examples.hard: Most of the students in my class are from Turkey, but two of them are from Japan.

examples.normal: Turkey is a big country between Europe and Asia.
examples.hard: Many people from Uzbekistan visit Turkey every year because the flights are short and cheap.

examples.normal: Canada is a very big country with long, cold winters.
examples.hard: My cousin moved to Canada five years ago, and now she works as a nurse in Toronto.

examples.normal: London is the capital of England and a very busy city.
examples.hard: He studied in England for two years, so his English is much better than mine.

examples.normal: Paris is in France, and it is a beautiful city.
examples.hard: We want to visit France next spring, because my wife has always wanted to see Paris.

examples.normal: Japan is in Asia, and Tokyo is its capital city.
examples.hard: Cars and phones from Japan are popular all over the world because of their good quality.

examples.normal: Spain is a sunny country with lovely beaches and food.
examples.hard: Every summer, thousands of tourists go to Spain to enjoy the hot weather and the sea.

examples.normal: Holland is famous for its flowers, bikes and old windmills.
examples.hard: In Holland, many people ride their bikes to work, even when the weather is cold and wet.

examples.normal: Please complete these sentences with 'am', 'is' or 'are'.
examples.hard: Try to make a short sentence about yourself, for example where you are from and what you do.

examples.normal: She smiled and said hello to everyone in the room.
examples.hard: Every morning, our neighbour says hello to us from her balcony while she waters her flowers.

examples.normal: "How are you?" "I'm fine, thanks. And you?"
examples.hard: When I met my old teacher in the street, she asked, "How are you? How is your family?"

examples.normal: "How is your mother?" "She's fine, thank you for asking."
examples.hard: I felt ill yesterday, but after a good night's sleep I'm fine again today.

examples.normal: "Would you like some tea?" "Yes, thanks. With sugar, please."
examples.hard: Thanks for driving me to the airport so early in the morning on a Sunday.

examples.normal: "How are you today?" "Very well, thank you. And you?"
examples.hard: My grandfather is eighty years old, but he is very well and still walks every day.

examples.normal: Lots of tourists visit Samarkand and Bukhara in the spring.
examples.hard: The old city is full of tourists in summer, so we prefer to go there in winter.

examples.normal: He is a businessman, and he often flies to China.
examples.hard: The businessmen at the next table were talking about prices and contracts all through lunch.

examples.normal: Is Susan at work today? No, she's on holiday this week.
examples.hard: When I'm on holiday, I turn off my work phone and try to forget about the office.

examples.normal: He is Scottish, but he lives and works in London.
examples.hard: You can hear that she is Scottish from her accent, even though she moved south years ago.

examples.normal: My neighbour is Turkish, and he cooks wonderful Turkish food.
examples.hard: Many Uzbek students can understand some Turkish because the two languages have a lot in common.

examples.normal: My new colleague is Japanese, and she speaks good English.
examples.hard: Japanese food is very healthy, and sushi has become popular in many countries around the world.

examples.normal: Gina is Italian, and she is from a small town near Rome.
examples.hard: We had dinner in an Italian restaurant last night, and the pizza was the best I've ever eaten.

examples.normal: Tom is American. He is from New York.
examples.hard: My American friend was surprised by how many people in Tashkent invited him to their homes for tea.

examples.normal: No, she isn't American. She's English, from London.
examples.hard: Jim is English, but he has lived in Turkey for so long that he speaks Turkish perfectly.

examples.normal: Are they Iranian? Yes, they are from Tehran.
examples.hard: Our neighbours are Iranian, and every spring they invite us to celebrate Navruz with them.

examples.easy: Is Jane Russian? No, she isn't.
examples.normal: My grandmother speaks Russian and Uzbek at home.
examples.hard: He reads Russian well, but he needs English for his new job at an international company.

examples.normal: Carlos is Mexican, and he works as a chef here.
examples.hard: We tried Mexican food for the first time last week, and it was much spicier than we expected.

examples.normal: Maria is Spanish. She's from Madrid, the capital of Spain.
examples.hard: My daughter is learning Spanish at school because she wants to study in Madrid one day.

examples.normal: Many of the students at this university are Chinese.
examples.hard: Chinese is a difficult language to learn, but more and more people are studying it today.

examples.normal: Betty is French, and she lives in Paris with her family.
examples.hard: I bought some French cheese at the market, but my children didn't like the strong smell.

examples.normal: China is a very big country with a long history.
examples.hard: A lot of the clothes and phones in our shops are made in China and sold all over the world.

examples.normal: Russia is the biggest country in the world.
examples.hard: My uncle worked in Russia for five years and sent money home to his family every month.

examples.normal: Scotland is in the north of the United Kingdom.
examples.hard: We spent a week walking in the mountains of Scotland, and it rained almost every day.

examples.normal: Please put the plates and glasses on the kitchen table.
examples.hard: We sat around the big table in my grandmother's house and talked until midnight.

examples.normal: There are four chairs around the table in our kitchen.
examples.hard: This old wooden chair is not very comfortable, but it belonged to my grandfather.

examples.normal: I like hot tea with a slice of lemon in winter.
examples.hard: When I have a cold, my mother makes me a drink with hot water, lemon and honey.

examples.normal: Can I have a knife and fork, please? I can't use chopsticks.
examples.hard: In many countries, people hold the fork in the left hand and the knife in the right.

examples.normal: I need a spoon for my soup. Where are the spoons?
examples.hard: Add two spoons of sugar to the flour, and mix everything together slowly with a wooden spoon.

examples.normal: I usually have two boiled eggs for breakfast every morning.
examples.hard: If you want to make a cake, you need three eggs, some flour, milk and sugar.

examples.normal: There are some oranges and apples in the bowl on the table.
examples.hard: In winter, I eat an orange every day because it has a lot of vitamin C.

examples.normal: There is a big clock on the wall in our classroom.
examples.hard: The clock in the kitchen is ten minutes fast, so we are never late for work.

examples.normal: My father gave me this watch when I finished university.
examples.hard: I don't wear a watch any more, because I always check the time on my phone.

examples.normal: I can't find my keys. Are they on the table?
examples.hard: Always keep a spare key with a neighbour, in case you lose yours or lock yourself out.

examples.normal: My parents live in a small house with a big garden.
examples.hard: They sold their old house in the village and bought a modern flat near the city centre.

examples.normal: My grandfather listens to the news on the radio every morning.
examples.hard: I usually listen to the radio in the car, because the traffic in the city is terrible.

examples.normal: Are these glasses clean? I want some water, please.
examples.hard: Doctors say you should drink at least six to eight glasses of water every day.

examples.normal: I go to work by bus because I don't have a car.
examples.hard: The buses in our city are cheap and modern, but they are always full in the morning.

examples.normal: Don't forget to take a towel to the swimming pool.
examples.hard: The hotel gives you fresh towels every day, but you can keep the same ones if you want.

examples.normal: I'm very tired. I want to go to bed early tonight.
examples.hard: Our son's room is small, so we bought him a bed with drawers underneath for his clothes.

examples.normal: Be careful with that knife! It is very sharp.
examples.hard: In the kitchen drawer there are three knives, six forks and a lot of small spoons.

examples.easy: What is it? It's a lorry.
examples.normal: Big lorries carry fruit and vegetables to the city every night.
examples.hard: My uncle drives a lorry, so he spends a lot of time on the road between Tashkent and Moscow.

examples.normal: There are some clean plates in the cupboard over there.
examples.hard: She filled my plate with plov twice, and I was too full to eat any dessert.

examples.normal: My mother keeps her keys and phone in her handbag.
examples.hard: She left her handbag on the bus, but luckily the driver found it and gave it back.

examples.normal: Would you like a cup of tea or coffee?
examples.hard: Every morning I drink a big cup of coffee before I check my emails and start work.

examples.easy: Are those shelves? Yes, they are.
examples.normal: The books are on the top shelf in the living room.
examples.hard: We need some new shelves in the kitchen, because there is no space for all the cups.

examples.normal: It's hot in here. Can you open the window, please?
examples.hard: From the window of our flat, we can see the mountains when the weather is clear.

examples.normal: Please close the door when you leave the room.
examples.hard: Someone knocked on the door at midnight, but when I opened it, nobody was there.

examples.normal: I eat an apple every day as a healthy snack.
examples.hard: Uzbekistan grows a lot of apples, and many of them are sold in Russia and Kazakhstan.

examples.normal: Her father works in a bank, and he drives a red car.
examples.hard: My father taught me to swim when I was six, and we still go swimming together.

examples.normal: Bart goes to his school by bus every morning.
examples.hard: The school near our house has a new sports hall, so the children play football there in winter.

examples.normal: My sister is a student, and her name is Lola.
examples.hard: My older sister lives abroad, so we talk on video every Sunday and share family news.

examples.normal: Jessica and Daisy live in a small apartment in the city.
examples.hard: Their apartment is on the ninth floor, so they have a wonderful view of the whole city.

examples.normal: What is your job? I'm a teacher at a primary school.
examples.hard: He lost his job last year, but now he has a better one with a much higher salary.

examples.normal: My grandmother grows tomatoes and flowers in her garden.
examples.hard: In summer we have dinner in the garden, under the old apple tree that my grandfather planted.

examples.normal: Their mother is a doctor, and she works at night.
examples.hard: My mother calls me every evening to ask how my day was and whether I have eaten.

examples.normal: It's very sunny today, so don't forget your hat.
examples.hard: He always wears his grandfather's old hat when he goes fishing at the lake on Sundays.

examples.normal: Our flat has two bedrooms, a kitchen and a living room.
examples.hard: The children share a bedroom now, but next year we want to move to a bigger flat.

examples.normal: We watch TV together in the living room every evening.
examples.hard: Our living room is the biggest room in the house, so all the guests sit there during holidays.

examples.normal: What is your favourite food? Mine is plov, of course.
examples.hard: My favourite season is autumn, because the weather is cool and the markets are full of fruit.

examples.normal: This is my brother. His name is Peter.
examples.hard: She forgot his name as soon as they were introduced, so she felt a bit embarrassed later.

examples.normal: My brother is a student in Hungary. He studies medicine.
examples.hard: My younger brother and I look very similar, so people often think we are twins.

examples.normal: My best friend and I meet at a café every Friday.
examples.hard: I met my best friend at university fifteen years ago, and we are still very close.

examples.normal: Their hobbies are gardening and walking in the mountains.
examples.hard: Since he retired, photography has become his favourite hobby, and he takes his camera everywhere.

examples.normal: Our daughter is eight, and she loves drawing and music.
examples.hard: My daughter wants to be a doctor, so she studies biology and chemistry very hard.

examples.normal: Don't forget your camera. The mountains are beautiful there.
examples.hard: I don't use a camera much any more, because the camera on my phone is just as good.

examples.normal: Children, please do your homework before you watch TV.
examples.hard: Our teacher gives us a lot of homework, so I usually study for two hours every evening.

examples.normal: I ride my bike to work when the weather is nice.
examples.hard: Someone stole my bike from outside the shop, so now I always lock it carefully.

examples.normal: My parents live in Fergana, and I visit them every month.
examples.hard: Her parents were very proud when she became the first doctor in the family.

examples.normal: My sister has long black hair, and she never cuts it short.
examples.hard: I need to get my hair cut before the wedding, but the hairdresser is busy all week.

examples.normal: We have two children, a boy and a girl.
examples.hard: On Saturday mornings, the children play in the park while their parents have tea nearby.

examples.normal: Her name is Susan Smith, and she is from London.
examples.hard: Please write your full name and phone number at the top of the form.

examples.normal: I can't open the door. Where are my keys?
examples.hard: He always leaves his car keys on the shelf by the door so he doesn't lose them.

examples.normal: Is this your umbrella here? No, my umbrella is red.
examples.hard: We have lived here for ten years, and we still love this quiet part of the city.

examples.normal: Look over there! That's my car next to the bus stop.
examples.hard: There was a small café on the corner, and we used to meet there after work.

examples.normal: Our flat has three rooms and a small kitchen.
examples.hard: The hotel room was clean and comfortable, but the window looked out onto a noisy street.

examples.normal: What are their jobs? They are teachers at the same school.
examples.hard: She wants to change her job, because she spends three hours on the bus every day.

examples.normal: The secretary answers the phone and writes the manager's letters.
examples.hard: Our new secretary is very organised, so the office runs much more smoothly than before.

examples.normal: He works as a cook in a busy restaurant in the centre.
examples.hard: My uncle was a cook in the army, so he can make plov for fifty people.

examples.normal: The receptionist at the hotel gave us the key to our room.
examples.hard: When you arrive at the clinic, tell the receptionist your name and the time of your appointment.

examples.normal: The cleaner comes to our office every evening after six.
examples.hard: These women are cleaners, and they start work at five in the morning before the shops open.

examples.normal: A policeman helped the old man cross the busy street.
examples.hard: When we got lost in the city, a friendly policeman showed us the way to our hotel.

examples.normal: My car is broken, so I'm taking it to the mechanic.
examples.hard: The mechanic said it would cost a lot to repair the old engine, so we sold the car.

examples.normal: The manager of the shop is very friendly and helpful.
examples.hard: If you have a problem with your order, you can speak to the manager at the front desk.

examples.normal: The waiter brought us the menu and two glasses of water.
examples.hard: We left the waiter a good tip, because he was so friendly and the service was very fast.

examples.normal: She is an air hostess, and she flies to Dubai every week.
examples.hard: The air hostess showed us how to fasten our seat belts before the plane took off.

examples.easy: Is Mr Cooper a taxi driver?
examples.normal: The taxi driver took us from the airport to our hotel.
examples.hard: Taxi drivers in big cities usually know every street, so they can avoid the traffic.

examples.easy: This is my case. It's heavy.
examples.normal: Where are your cases? Are they in the car?
examples.hard: My case was too heavy at the airport, so I had to take out some of my clothes.

examples.normal: Good evening, everyone! Welcome to our English class tonight.
examples.hard: The hotel receptionist smiled and said, "Good evening, sir. What is your name, please?"

examples.normal: Excuse me, sir, is this your umbrella on the chair?
examples.hard: The waiter said, "Your table is ready, sir. Please follow me to the window."

units.name: Lesson 7 - Adjectives and telling the time

examples.normal: A good dictionary is very useful when you learn English.
examples.hard: My teacher gave me some useful advice about how to remember new words more easily.

examples.normal: Although he is rich, he lives in a very small flat.
examples.hard: Although the hotel was cheap, the rooms were clean and the staff were very friendly.

examples.normal: I assume the shop is closed, because the lights are off.
examples.hard: We assumed the train would be on time, so we were surprised when it arrived an hour late.

examples.normal: Let's assume the trip costs five hundred dollars per person.
examples.hard: Let's assume that twenty people come to the party; then we will need at least five big cakes.

examples.normal: What colour are her eyes? I think they are green.
examples.hard: What colour do you want to paint the kitchen walls, white or light yellow?

examples.normal: In English, an adjective usually comes before the noun.
examples.hard: Words like 'tired', 'rich' and 'expensive' are adjectives, because they describe people and things.

examples.normal: What colour is your hair? It's dark brown.
examples.hard: Marge Simpson has very tall blue hair, so everyone recognises her immediately.

examples.normal: She is wearing a beautiful red dress at the party.
examples.hard: When the traffic light turns red, all the cars must stop and wait for green.

examples.normal: He is a good doctor, and all his patients like him.
examples.hard: It was a good idea to leave early, because the roads were empty and we arrived on time.

examples.normal: My brother has blue eyes, but my eyes are brown.
examples.hard: We painted the bedroom walls light blue, because it is a calm and relaxing colour.

examples.normal: Is David strong? Yes, he can carry the heavy boxes.
examples.hard: You need to be strong to work as a porter, because you carry heavy bags all day.

examples.normal: Please read the text and then do Task 1.
examples.hard: Our manager gave each of us a different task, and we had to finish everything by Friday.

examples.normal: The test was easy, so everyone in the class passed.
examples.hard: Learning to drive was not easy for me, but after many lessons I finally passed the test.

examples.normal: The lesson starts at eight o'clock every morning.
examples.hard: I usually wake up at seven o'clock, but on Sundays I stay in bed until nine.

examples.normal: The bus leaves at twenty past seven, so we must hurry.
examples.hard: The film started at half past eight, but we arrived at ten past nine and missed the beginning.

examples.normal: The train leaves at twenty to nine, so please don't be late.
examples.hard: I usually finish work at five to six and then walk to the bus stop near my office.

examples.normal: We have a short break at quarter to eleven every day.
examples.hard: The meeting started at quarter past nine and finished more than two hours later, at half past eleven.

examples.normal: We have lunch at half past twelve, then go back to work.
examples.hard: Half of the students in my class are from Tashkent, and the other half are from other cities.

examples.normal: The bus stop is only five minutes from my house.
examples.hard: The doctor will see you in a few minutes, so please sit down and fill in this form.

examples.normal: Is that man angry? No, he isn't. He is tired.
examples.hard: After working twelve hours in the hospital, the nurses were too tired to talk.

examples.normal: This laptop is light, so I can carry it everywhere.
examples.hard: Take a light jacket with you, because it can get cool in the mountains in the evening.

examples.normal: Is my handbag light? No, it isn't. It's heavy.
examples.hard: The suitcase was so heavy that the porter needed help to carry it up the stairs.

examples.normal: Are those taxi drivers thirsty? No, they are hungry.
examples.hard: We were very hungry after the long walk, so we ordered two big plates of plov.

examples.normal: I have a new phone, and it takes great photos.
examples.hard: We moved into a new flat last month, but we still don't have any furniture in the kitchen.

examples.normal: Is the house cheap? No, it isn't. It's expensive.
examples.hard: Fruit is very cheap at the market in summer, so we buy a lot and make jam.

examples.normal: This restaurant is good, but it is too expensive for us.
examples.hard: Flights are always more expensive in summer, so we usually travel in spring or autumn.

examples.normal: Are these women tall? No, they aren't. They're short.
examples.hard: The woman at the information desk was very helpful and showed us where to buy tickets.

examples.normal: Their house is very big, and it has a lovely garden.
examples.hard: My grandparents built this house fifty years ago, and the whole family still meets here.

examples.normal: This shop sells many different kinds of tea and coffee.
examples.hard: The students in this class are from different cities, but they all want to learn English.

examples.normal: There is a dirty ashtray on the table in the hall.
examples.hard: Smoking is not allowed in the hotel, so you won't find an ashtray in any of the rooms.

examples.normal: The fastest runner finished the race in ten seconds.
examples.hard: The lights went out for a few seconds, and then everything in the house came back on.

examples.normal: It is very hot here at midday, so people stay inside.
examples.hard: The shop closes at midday on Saturdays, so we need to buy everything in the morning.

examples.normal: I usually take my lunch break at noon every day.
examples.hard: Please check out of your hotel room by twelve noon, or you will have to pay extra.

examples.easy: We went to bed at midnight.
examples.normal: The last metro train leaves the station just before midnight.
examples.hard: We watched films and talked until midnight, so we were very tired at work the next day.

examples.normal: The cat is fat because it eats all day and sleeps.
examples.hard: The vet said our dog was too fat and told us to give it less food and more exercise.

examples.normal: Is Carol short? No, she isn't. She is tall.
examples.hard: He is short, but he is one of the best basketball players in our university team.

examples.normal: The porter isn't short. He is a tall, strong man.
examples.hard: Our son is only fourteen, but he is already taller than his father and his uncle.

examples.normal: After a long illness, my grandfather is still quite weak.
examples.hard: She felt weak and tired after the flu, so the doctor told her to stay at home for a week.

examples.normal: Are those businessmen poor? No, they are very rich.
examples.hard: He became rich by selling cars, but he still lives in the same small house as before.

examples.normal: Please put the clean plates in the cupboard.
examples.hard: My grandmother always fills my plate with food, even when I tell her I'm not hungry.

examples.normal: The bus is full, so we need to wait for another.
examples.hard: The fridge was full of food, because we were expecting twenty guests for my birthday.

examples.normal: My wife keeps her phone and keys in her handbag.
examples.hard: She bought an expensive leather handbag in Istanbul, and she carries it everywhere.

examples.normal: The porter carried our cases to the room on the fifth floor.
examples.hard: At the station, a porter helped the old woman carry her heavy bags to the train.

examples.normal: Can you describe your father? Is he tall or short?
examples.hard: The police asked her to describe the man, but she only remembered his red jacket.

examples.normal: Is that man angry? No, he isn't angry. He's tired.
examples.hard: The man who lives next door is a doctor, and he always helps us when the children are ill.

examples.normal: My boss was angry because I was late for the meeting.
examples.hard: She was angry with her son because he broke the window and then lied about it.

examples.easy: I'm thirsty. Can I have water?
examples.normal: It's very hot today, so everyone is thirsty.
examples.hard: After playing football for two hours in the sun, the boys were hot and very thirsty.

examples.normal: Would you like a cup of tea with lemon?
examples.hard: My grandfather drinks at least six cups of green tea every day, even in summer.

examples.normal: I don't like this lamp. I think it's really ugly.
examples.hard: The new shopping centre looks quite ugly from outside, but it is beautiful inside.

examples.normal: The little girl in the red dress is very beautiful.
examples.hard: The girl next door is only ten, but she already plays the piano very well.

examples.normal: The secretary works in the office from nine to five.
examples.hard: Please call my secretary tomorrow morning, and she will give you a time for the meeting.

examples.normal: Is your book thin? No, it isn't. It's thick.
examples.hard: In winter, I wear a thick jacket and warm boots, because it is very cold outside.

examples.normal: Please take a clean towel from the bathroom shelf.
examples.hard: Don't forget to take a big towel to the beach, because the sand is very hot.

examples.normal: Can I have a glass of water, please?
examples.hard: He filled the glasses with cold juice and carried them carefully into the garden.

examples.normal: Can you tell me about that man? Is he rich?
examples.hard: My grandmother loves to tell us stories about her life in the village when she was young.

examples.normal: My husband is a good cook, and he cooks every Sunday.
examples.hard: She works as a cook in a big hotel, and she cooks for more than two hundred guests a day.

examples.normal: Is this your case? It's very heavy, isn't it?
examples.hard: I always pack my case the night before a trip, so I don't forget anything important.

examples.normal: She is sad because her best friend is moving away.
examples.hard: It was a sad day for everyone when our favourite teacher left the school.

examples.normal: Is the cup full? No, it isn't. It's empty.
examples.hard: The streets were empty at five in the morning, so we drove to the airport very quickly.

examples.normal: Those women are tall and thin, like fashion models.
examples.hard: He was very thin after his illness, so his mother cooked his favourite food every day.

examples.normal: Is your umbrella new? No, it isn't. It's old.
examples.hard: We still use my grandmother's old table, although it is more than sixty years old.

units.name: Lesson 8 - There is / there are at home

examples.normal: There is a big supermarket near our flat.
examples.hard: There is a small café on the corner where you can get very good coffee and cake.

examples.easy: The plates are in the cupboard.
examples.normal: There are some cups and glasses in the kitchen cupboard.
examples.hard: We keep the cleaning things in the cupboard under the sink, away from the children.

examples.easy: Is there milk in the fridge?
examples.normal: Put the meat and the milk in the fridge, please.
examples.hard: Our old fridge is very noisy, so we want to buy a new one before the summer.

examples.easy: The towels are in the bathroom.
examples.normal: Our flat has one bathroom, and it is quite small.
examples.hard: In the morning, everyone in my family wants to use the bathroom at the same time.

examples.easy: The fridge is in the kitchen.
examples.normal: My mother is in the kitchen, cooking dinner for us.
examples.hard: We usually eat breakfast in the kitchen, because it is warm and close to the cooker.

examples.normal: Is there a telephone in your living room? Yes, there is.
examples.hard: My grandmother still uses the old telephone in the hall to call her friends every evening.

examples.normal: The soup is on the cooker. It's still hot.
examples.hard: We bought a new gas cooker for the kitchen, because the old one didn't work well.

examples.normal: There is a big television in our living room.
examples.hard: My father watches the football on television every Saturday evening with his friends.

examples.normal: Is there a sofa in the living room? No, there isn't.
examples.hard: After a long day at work, I like to lie on the sofa and read a good book.

examples.easy: There are apples in the fridge.
examples.normal: There are some glasses on the shelf in the kitchen.
examples.hard: There are more than thirty students in our class, so the room is always crowded.

examples.easy: The pans are in the kitchen.
examples.normal: Wash the pans after dinner, please. They are very dirty.
examples.hard: She used a big pan to make plov for all the guests at the wedding.

examples.easy: The cat is under the table.
examples.normal: Is there a cupboard under the sink? Yes, there is.
examples.hard: I found my lost keys under the sofa when I was cleaning the living room on Sunday.

examples.easy: The knives are in the sink.
examples.normal: There are a lot of dirty plates in the kitchen sink.
examples.hard: Don't leave the dirty dishes in the sink all night, or the kitchen will smell bad.

examples.normal: There is a bottle of water on the shelf.
examples.hard: Please don't throw plastic bottles in the street; put them in the special bins instead.

examples.easy: There are chairs on the balcony.
examples.normal: We drink tea on the balcony on warm summer evenings.
examples.hard: Our flat has a small balcony, where my wife grows tomatoes and flowers every summer.

examples.easy: There are magazines on the table.
examples.normal: Are there any magazines in the living room? Yes, there are.
examples.hard: While I was waiting at the dentist's, I read an interesting magazine article about travel.

examples.easy: There is a tall boy here.
examples.normal: There are some boys in the garden playing football.
examples.hard: The boy next door is only twelve, but he already speaks three languages very well.

examples.easy: Is there a hotel near here?
examples.normal: Are there any businessmen in the hotel? Yes, there are.
examples.hard: We stayed in a small hotel near the old city, and the breakfast every morning was excellent.

examples.easy: There is a cat under the table.
examples.normal: Our cat sleeps on the sofa in the living room all day.
examples.hard: We found a little cat in the street, and now it is part of our family.

examples.normal: Look at the photo. Is there a sofa in the room?
examples.hard: If you look at the map carefully, you will see a small hotel next to the station.

examples.normal: There are three rooms and a big kitchen in our flat.
examples.hard: They live in a modern flat on the fifth floor, with a beautiful view of the park.
